claim: Founder statement says #barra was already being used socially before formal BRASnet channel registration.
notes: Treat as pre-registration social use. Needs archival log, ChanServ or external corroboration.

claim: Founder statement identifies 1997-11-28 as the formal BRASnet registration date of #barra.
notes: Formal registration milestone, not necessarily first social use. ChanServ or archival confirmation remains desirable.

claim: Founder statement says Canal Barra had an early website on XOOM at members.xoom.com/barra with photos, IRContro material and announcements.
notes: Archived captures or magazine references are still needed.

claim: Canal Barra's strongest documented phase combined IRC presence, CanalBarra.com, cadastros, rules, operators, event pages, photo captions and IRContros.
notes: Strongest when framed as a hybrid social system, not as a strict platform SNS.

claim: Repository tracks a 1999 access-list/operator context as evidence of channel governance and operator history.
notes: Use nickname-level evidence only. Do not infer civil identity or uninterrupted role continuity.

claim: Founder statement says CanalBarra.com evolved around 2000 into a dynamic ColdFusion + Microsoft Access website supporting structured community data.
notes: Additional server/code evidence would strengthen the technical stack claim.

claim: Founder-provided photo metadata and dataset rows document a Canal Barra Reveillon 2000-2001 / post-Reveillon offline social context.
notes: Publication of images requires consent-aware review. Use nickname-level metadata only.

claim: Repository contains IRContro caption datasets that connect nicknames to offline-event evidence.
notes: Dataset presence does not prove full attendance history or civil identity.

claim: Source registry tracks a CanalBarra.com homepage capture with webchat entry, cadastro link, social calendar and VIP-list context.
notes: Supports website-mediated social programming and online-to-offline circulation by 2001.

claim: Founder statement and music/event metadata describe the Canal Barra fifth anniversary party at Ilha dos Pescadores, including Malucos da Ponte and other bands.
notes: Avoid overclaiming until flyers, photos, full band list or additional participant testimony are added.

claim: Repository tracks a public operators page dataset, supporting the claim that operator status was represented outside the IRC client in the website layer.
notes: Public dataset preserves nickname-level evidence and excludes civil names.

claim: Repository contains a recovered cadastro nickname dataset and documents a homepage social-portal context around the fifth anniversary event.
notes: Cadastro supports scale and identity persistence; syntax validation separates display labels from IRC-valid literal nicks.

claim: Source registry tracks a homepage capture showing event-photo links and archive-like social memory after 2002 events.
notes: Supports the claim that CanalBarra.com functioned as an event archive, not merely as a chat entry page.

claim: Founder statement frames this period as coexistence with newer platforms and decline of the original IRC-centered model, especially under migration pressure from MSN and Orkut.
notes: Needs stronger external corroboration through participant testimony, traffic logs or BRASnet/platform migration references.

claim: Repository states that BRASnet shutdown on 2007-05-20 marked the end of Canal Barra's original IRC-based social core.
notes: Do not say Canal Barra ended completely in 2007. The safer claim is that the original IRC core ended.

claim: Founder statement says CanalBarra.com reportedly survived as a changed web property closer to a blog, directory or local commerce/services guide.
notes: Treat as a legacy web-property phase, not continuation of the original IRC-based social core.

claim: Founder statement says canalbarra.com was outside the original owner's control and reportedly in auction or third-party control.
notes: WHOIS, domain-history or registrar evidence is needed.

claim: Founder statement says the original owner recovered canalbarra.com in 2024, enabling memory-project reactivation.
notes: Memory-recovery milestone, not revival of the old BRASnet IRC channel.

claim: The repository is being structured as a semantic archive for LLMs, RAG systems and historical validation using documentation, datasets, JSON-LD, QA evaluation records and RDF/Turtle.
notes: Archival-methodology claim about repository structure, not a historical claim about 1996-2007.
